questions.question:
Ravi plans to better support a section of roof truss $ABC$ which sits on top of a wall $CBDE$, by installing two steel ropes $AF$ and $BF$, as shown in the diagram. The wall $CBDE$ sits on the ground, which is a level surface. The apex $A$ of the roof is $11$ m above the ground (so $AE=11$) and the other end of the roof truss (point $B$) is $8$ m above the ground (so $BD=8$). Ravi installs a steel rope from $B$ to a peg at point $F$, which is located at ground level, and another steel rope from $A$ to $F$. The angle of elevation from $F$ to $B$ is $65^\circ$ and the angle of elevation from $F$ to $A$ is $55^\circ$.

Show that $DF=8\cot65^\circ$.
questions.answer: In the right-angled triangle $BDF$ (right angle at $D$), $\tan65^\circ=\dfrac{BD}{DF}=\dfrac{8}{DF}$, so $DF=\dfrac{8}{\tan65^\circ}=8\cot65^\circ$.

questions.question:
Ravi plans to better support a section of roof truss $ABC$ which sits on top of a wall $CBDE$, by installing two steel ropes $AF$ and $BF$, as shown in the diagram. The wall $CBDE$ sits on the ground, which is a level surface. The apex $A$ of the roof is $11$ m above the ground (so $AE=11$) and the other end of the roof truss (point $B$) is $8$ m above the ground (so $BD=8$). Ravi installs a steel rope from $B$ to a peg at point $F$, which is located at ground level, and another steel rope from $A$ to $F$. The angle of elevation from $F$ to $B$ is $65^\circ$ and the angle of elevation from $F$ to $A$ is $55^\circ$. From part (a), $DF=8\cot65^\circ$.

The area of $\triangle DFE$ is $12.34\ \text{m}^2$. Show that $\angle DFE=59^\circ12'$.
questions.answer:
In the right-angled triangle $AEF$ (right angle at $E$), $\tan55^\circ=\dfrac{11}{EF}$, so $EF=11\cot55^\circ$.

Area of $\triangle DFE$: $\tfrac12(DF)(EF)\sin\angle DFE=12.34$
$$\tfrac12(8\cot65^\circ)(11\cot55^\circ)\sin\angle DFE=12.34\Rightarrow\sin\angle DFE=\frac{12.34\tan65^\circ\tan55^\circ}{44}\approx0.8589.$$
So $\angle DFE=\sin^{-1}(0.8589)\approx59^\circ12'$ (to the nearest minute, taking the acute angle as in the diagram).

questions.question: Ravi plans to better support a section of roof truss $ABC$ which sits on top of a wall $CBDE$, by installing two steel ropes $AF$ and $BF$, as shown in the diagram. The wall $CBDE$ sits on the ground, which is a level surface. The apex $A$ of the roof is $11$ m above the ground (so $AE=11$) and the other end of the roof truss (point $B$) is $8$ m above the ground (so $BD=8$). Ravi installs a steel rope from $B$ to a peg at point $F$, which is located at ground level, and another steel rope from $A$ to $F$. The angle of elevation from $F$ to $B$ is $65^\circ$ and the angle of elevation from $F$ to $A$ is $55^\circ$. Given $DF=8\cot65^\circ$, $EF=11\cot55^\circ$ and $\angle DFE=59^\circ12'$, find the slant length of the roof truss $AB$, correct to two decimal places.
questions.answer:
In $\triangle DFE$ (cosine rule): $DE^2=DF^2+EF^2-2(DF)(EF)\cos\angle DFE$, with $DF\approx3.7305$, $EF\approx7.7023$:
$$DE^2=(8\cot65^\circ)^2+(11\cot55^\circ)^2-2(8\cot65^\circ)(11\cot55^\circ)\cos59^\circ12'\Rightarrow DE\approx6.6194.$$
$BCED$ is a rectangle, so $BC=DE\approx6.6194$ m, and $AC=11-8=3$ m. In the right-angled triangle $ABC$:
$$AB^2=BC^2+AC^2=6.6194^2+3^2\Rightarrow AB\approx7.27\ \text{m}.$$

questions.question:
Emma is plane-spotting at a sea-level point $E$. She can see her house $H$ on a bearing of 030°T, and a plane $A$ directly above her house at an angle of elevation of 20°. From $A$, the plane travels at a constant altitude of 900 m on a bearing of 225°T to a point $B$, 1700 m away, which is directly above a landmark $L$.

Determine the bearing and the angle of elevation of the aircraft at $B$ from Emma's position $E$.
questions.answer:
In $\triangle EHA$: $EH = \dfrac{900}{\tan 20^\circ} \approx 2472.73$ m.

In $\triangle EHL$ (at ground level, $HL = 1700$): the bearing of $E$ from $H$ is 210° and of $L$ from $H$ is 225°, so $\angle EHL = 15^\circ$.
$$EL^2 = 1700^2 + 2472.73^2 - 2(1700)(2472.73)\cos 15^\circ \Rightarrow EL \approx 939.99 \text{ m}.$$
Angle of elevation of $B$: $\tan\alpha = \dfrac{900}{939.99} \Rightarrow \alpha \approx 44^\circ$.

Bearing: in $\triangle EHL$, $\dfrac{\sin\beta}{1700} = \dfrac{\sin 15^\circ}{939.99}$ where $\beta = \angle HEL$, giving $\beta \approx 27.9^\circ$ (acute, since it is not opposite the longest side). The bearing of $L$ (and $B$) from $E$ is $30^\circ - 27.9^\circ \approx 002^\circ$T.

questions.question:
Two hikers, Liam ($L$) and Sophie ($S$), are on a flat valley floor and can both see the top $E$ of Eagle Peak, which is 1800 m directly above the point $B$ on the valley floor. From Liam, the peak is on a bearing of 072° with an angle of elevation of 18°. From Sophie, the peak is on a bearing of 118° with an angle of elevation of 27°.

Find the distance between Liam and Sophie and determine the bearing of Liam from Sophie.
questions.answer:
$LB = \dfrac{1800}{\tan 18^\circ} \approx 5539.8$ m and $SB = \dfrac{1800}{\tan 27^\circ} \approx 3532.7$ m.

From $B$, Liam is on a bearing of $252^\circ$ and Sophie on $298^\circ$, so $\angle LBS = 46^\circ$.
$$LS^2 = 5539.8^2 + 3532.7^2 - 2(5539.8)(3532.7)\cos 46^\circ \Rightarrow LS \approx 3997 \text{ m}.$$
For the bearing, find $\angle LSB$. Since $LB$ is the longest side, the angle opposite it may be obtuse, so use the cosine rule:
$$\cos\angle LSB = \frac{LS^2 + SB^2 - LB^2}{2\cdot LS\cdot SB} \approx -0.079 \Rightarrow \angle LSB \approx 94.5^\circ.$$
The bearing of $B$ from $S$ is $118^\circ$, and $L$ is a further $94.5^\circ$ clockwise, so the bearing of Liam from Sophie is about $212.5^\circ \approx 213^\circ$T.

(The paper's solution used the sine rule and took the acute angle $85^\circ$, giving $203^\circ$; the angle is in fact obtuse.)

questions.question:
The diagram shows $AB$ and $CD$, two vertical towers of height $h$ and $2h$ metres respectively. $AB$ is south of tower $CD$, at a distance $d$ metres from it ($AC = d$). $O$ is a point on the ground, west of $CD$ and at the same level as $A$ and $C$. The distance $OC$ is $\frac34 d$ metres. The angle of elevation of $B$ from $O$ is $30^\circ$ and the angle of elevation of $D$ from $O$ is $\alpha$.

Show that $h = \dfrac38 d\tan\alpha$.
questions.answer: In right-angled triangle $OCD$: $\tan\alpha = \dfrac{CD}{OC} = \dfrac{2h}{\frac34 d} = \dfrac{8h}{3d}$, so $h = \dfrac{3d\tan\alpha}{8}$.

questions.question:
The diagram shows $AB$ and $CD$, two vertical towers of height $h$ and $2h$ metres respectively. $AB$ is south of tower $CD$, at a distance $d$ metres from it ($AC = d$). $O$ is a point on the ground, west of $CD$ and at the same level as $A$ and $C$. The distance $OC$ is $\frac34 d$ metres. The angle of elevation of $B$ from $O$ is $30^\circ$ and the angle of elevation of $D$ from $O$ is $\alpha$. It is known that $h = \dfrac38 d\tan\alpha$.

By finding another expression for $h$, find the angle of elevation $\alpha$ to the nearest minute.
questions.answer:
In right-angled triangle $OAB$: $\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{h}{OA}$, so $h = \dfrac{OA}{\sqrt3}$.

$O$ is west of $C$ and $A$ is south of $C$, so $\angle OCA = 90^\circ$ and by Pythagoras
$$OA^2 = d^2 + \left(\frac{3d}{4}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{16}d^2 \;\Rightarrow\; OA = \frac54 d.$$
So $h = \dfrac{5d}{4\sqrt3}$. Equating with $h = \dfrac{3d}{8}\tan\alpha$:
$$\tan\alpha = \frac{5}{4\sqrt3} \times \frac{8}{3} = \frac{10}{3\sqrt3} \approx 1.9245,$$
so $\alpha \approx 62^\circ 33'$.

questions.question:
In the diagram, $A$, $B$ and $C$ are three points on level ground and $P$ is a point vertically above $C$. In triangle $ABC$, $AB=20$ km, $\angle CAB=40^\circ$ and $\angle ACB=120^\circ$. Also $PA=9.12$ km and $PB=15.52$ km.

Find the length of $AC$, correct to the nearest $0.1$ km.
questions.answer:
$\angle ABC=180^\circ-40^\circ-120^\circ=20^\circ$. By the sine rule in $\triangle ABC$:
$$\frac{AC}{\sin20^\circ}=\frac{20}{\sin120^\circ}\ \Rightarrow\ AC=\frac{20\sin20^\circ}{\sin120^\circ}\approx7.8986\approx7.9\text{ km}.$$

questions.question:
In the diagram, $A$, $B$ and $C$ are three points on level ground and $P$ is a point vertically above $C$. In triangle $ABC$, $AB=20$ km, $\angle CAB=40^\circ$ and $\angle ACB=120^\circ$. Also $PA=9.12$ km and $PB=15.52$ km. The length $AC\approx7.9$ km.

Find the angle of elevation of $P$ from $A$, correct to the nearest minute.
questions.answer:
$PC$ is vertical, so $\triangle PCA$ is right-angled at $C$ and the angle of elevation is $\theta=\angle PAC$:
$$\cos\theta=\frac{AC}{PA}=\frac{7.9}{9.12}\ \Rightarrow\ \theta\approx29^\circ59'.$$
*Note: the paper uses the rounded value $AC=7.9$; using the unrounded $AC=7.8986\ldots$ gives $\theta\approx30^\circ0'$.*

$$\angle APB\approx105^\circ34'.$$

questions.question: Two coastal observation stations $A$ and $B$ are 500 metres apart, with $B$ due east of $A$. The point $C$, directly below a rescue drone, has bearing $050^\circ$ from $A$ and bearing $305^\circ$ from $B$. The drone is at $D$, vertically above $C$. The angle of elevation of $D$ from $A$ is $32^\circ$. Find $AD$, correct to the nearest metre.
questions.answer: In the horizontal triangle $ABC$: $\angle A=90^\circ-50^\circ=40^\circ$, $\angle B=35^\circ$, so $\angle C=105^\circ$. Sine rule: $AC=\dfrac{500\sin35^\circ}{\sin105^\circ}$. In the vertical triangle $ACD$, $\cos32^\circ=\dfrac{AC}{AD}$, so $AD=\dfrac{500\sin35^\circ}{\sin105^\circ\cos32^\circ}\approx350.1$, so $AD=350$ m.

questions.question: The rectangular prism below has $BF=5$ cm, $FG=9$ cm, $GH=12$ cm, $AH=\sqrt{106}$ cm and $AF=13$ cm, as shown in the diagram. Find the size of $\angle HAF$, correct to the nearest degree.
questions.answer: In the base, $HF=\sqrt{12^2+9^2}=15$ cm. In $\triangle AHF$, by the cosine rule: $\cos\angle HAF=\dfrac{(\sqrt{106})^2+13^2-15^2}{2\times\sqrt{106}\times13}=\dfrac{106+169-225}{26\sqrt{106}}=\dfrac{50}{26\sqrt{106}}\approx0.1868$. So $\angle HAF\approx79^\circ$.

questions.question: A triangular prism $ABCDEF$ is made as a door wedge. It has a height of $22$ mm and a width of $60$ mm. The angle of the wedge is $18^\circ$ (the angle $EAD$). Find the angle, correct to the nearest degree, between the diagonal $BE$ and the diagonal of the base $ABCD$ (the base is a rectangle with $AB=60$ mm, and $DE=22$ mm is perpendicular to the base).
questions.answer:
In $\triangle EDA$ (right angle at $D$): $\tan18^\circ=\dfrac{22}{AD}\Rightarrow AD=\dfrac{22}{\tan18^\circ}=67.71$ mm.

The base diagonal is $BD$: $BD=\sqrt{60^2+67.71^2}=90.47$ mm.

$E$ is directly above $D$, so the angle between $BE$ and the base diagonal $BD$ is $\angle EBD$ in right triangle $EDB$:
$$\tan\theta=\frac{22}{90.47}\Rightarrow\theta=13.7^\circ\approx14^\circ.$$

questions.question:
Prove that, for $0 \le x \le 1$,
$$\cos^{-1}\left(\sqrt{x}\right)=\frac12\cos^{-1}\left(2x-1\right)$$
questions.answer:
Let $\theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\sqrt{x}\right)$. Since $0 \le \sqrt{x} \le 1$, we have $0 \le \theta \le \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and $\cos\theta = \sqrt{x}$.

Using the double-angle formula,
$$\cos 2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 = 2\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^2 - 1 = 2x - 1.$$

Since $0 \le 2\theta \le \pi$, which is the range of $\cos^{-1}$, it follows that
$$2\theta = \cos^{-1}(2x-1) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \cos^{-1}\left(\sqrt{x}\right) = \theta = \frac12\cos^{-1}(2x-1). \qquad \blacksquare$$

(The range check is essential: $\cos 2\theta = 2x-1$ alone only gives $2\theta = \cos^{-1}(2x-1)$ because $2\theta$ lies in $[0,\pi]$.)

questions.question:
(b) Using the result $\cos(A-B) - \cos(A+B) = 2\sin A \sin B$ from part (a), or otherwise, prove by mathematical induction that, for $n \ge 1$,
$$\sin\theta + \sin(3\theta) + \cdots + \sin\big((2n-1)\theta\big) = \frac{\sin^2(n\theta)}{\sin\theta}.$$
questions.answer:
(Assume $\sin\theta \ne 0$, so the right-hand side is defined.)

**Base case $n=1$.** LHS $= \sin\theta$. RHS $= \dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta} = \sin\theta$. True for $n=1$.

**Inductive step.** Assume true for $n=k$:
$$\sin\theta + \sin 3\theta + \cdots + \sin\big((2k-1)\theta\big) = \frac{\sin^2(k\theta)}{\sin\theta}.$$
Prove true for $n=k+1$, i.e. that the sum up to $\sin\big((2k+1)\theta\big)$ equals $\dfrac{\sin^2\big((k+1)\theta\big)}{\sin\theta}$.

$$\text{LHS} = \frac{\sin^2(k\theta)}{\sin\theta} + \sin\big((2k+1)\theta\big) = \frac{\sin^2(k\theta) + \sin\theta\,\sin\big((2k+1)\theta\big)}{\sin\theta}.$$

By part (a) with $A = (2k+1)\theta$, $B = \theta$:
$$\sin\big((2k+1)\theta\big)\sin\theta = \tfrac12\big[\cos(2k\theta) - \cos\big((2k+2)\theta\big)\big].$$
Also $\sin^2(k\theta) = \tfrac12\big[1 - \cos(2k\theta)\big]$. So the numerator is
$$\tfrac12\big[1-\cos(2k\theta)\big] + \tfrac12\big[\cos(2k\theta) - \cos\big(2(k+1)\theta\big)\big] = \tfrac12\big[1 - \cos\big(2(k+1)\theta\big)\big] = \sin^2\big((k+1)\theta\big).$$

Hence LHS $= \dfrac{\sin^2\big((k+1)\theta\big)}{\sin\theta}$ = RHS, so the result is true for $n=k+1$.

By mathematical induction, the result is true for all integers $n \ge 1$.

prev.question: Show that $\cos(A-B) - \cos(A+B) = 2\sin A \sin B$.
prev.answer: $$\begin{aligned}\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B) &= (\cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B) - (\cos A\cos B - \sin A \sin B)\\ &= 2\sin A\sin B\end{aligned}$$

questions.question: The diagram shows the graph of $P(x) = a(x+b)(x+c)(x+d)^2$. Which of the following is a possible set of values for $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$?
questions.answer:
Single zeros at $x = -3$ and $x = -1$, and a double zero (touching) at $x = 2$, so $P(x) = a(x+3)(x+1)(x-2)^2$: $b, c = 3, 1$ and $d = -2$.
$P(0) = a \cdot 3 \cdot 1 \cdot 4 = 12a = -24$, so $a = -2$ (negative leading coefficient, matching the shape).

questions.question: $f(x)$ is an odd function and $f(-1) < 0$. Which graph (A–D) could show $y = f(-|x|)$?
questions.answer: $y = f(-|x|)$ is even (symmetric about the $y$-axis). For $x > 0$ it equals $f(-x) = -f(x)$; since $f(1) = -f(-1) > 0$, the graph is below the axis for $x > 0$ near $x = 1$, and by symmetry also for $x < 0$. Only C fits.

questions.question: Which is a correct anti-derivative for $\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{4 - 9x^2}}$?
questions.answer: $$\int \frac{6}{\sqrt{4 - 9x^2}}\,dx = \int \frac{2}{\sqrt{\frac{4}{9} - x^2}}\,dx = 2\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3x}{2}\right) + C.$$

questions.question: Two hot bodies, A and B, have temperatures of 120°C and 80°C at $t = 0$ seconds. The temperature of the surroundings is 40°C. Assuming Newton's law of cooling, the ratio of the rate of cooling of body A to body B at $t = 0$ seconds is:
Which of the following differential equations yields the direction field shown?
questions.answer: Along the $y$-axis ($x = 0$) the slopes are 0, so the numerator contains the factor $x$: A or C. To decide, test a point on the line $y = -x$, e.g. $(-2, 2)$: A gives $\dfrac{-2\cos 0}{2} = -1$ while C gives $\dfrac{-2\sin 0}{2} = 0$. The field has a clearly negative slope there, so the answer is A. (Check: at $(2, 0.5)$, A gives $4\cos 2.5 \approx -3.2$, matching the steep negative slopes.)

questions.question: A particle has position vector $\mathbf{r}(t) = \cos^{-1}(t)\,\mathbf{i} + \sin^{-1}(t)\,\mathbf{j}$. The distance travelled by the particle in the interval $[-1, 1]$ is closest to
questions.answer:
Since $\cos^{-1}t + \sin^{-1}t = \frac{\pi}{2}$, the path is the straight line $x + y = \frac{\pi}{2}$, traced once from $(\pi, -\frac{\pi}{2})$ at $t = -1$ to $(0, \frac{\pi}{2})$ at $t = 1$.
Distance $= \sqrt{\pi^2 + \pi^2} = \sqrt{2}\pi$.

questions.question: Given $\cos(3\theta) = 4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta$, which of the following is the simplified form of $\cos^{-1}(4x^3 - 3x)$?
questions.answer:
Let $x = \cos\theta$ with $\theta = \cos^{-1}x \in [0, \pi]$. Then $4x^3 - 3x = \cos 3\theta$, so $\cos^{-1}(4x^3 - 3x) = \cos^{-1}(\cos 3\theta) = 3\theta = 3\cos^{-1}x$, provided $3\theta \in [0, \pi]$.

Note: this only holds for $\frac{1}{2} \le x \le 1$ (e.g. at $x = 0$ the left side is $\frac{\pi}{2}$ but $3\cos^{-1}0 = \frac{3\pi}{2}$). C is the intended answer.

questions.question: How many integers do **not** satisfy the inequality $3|x - 1| + x^2 - 7 > 0$?
questions.answer:
For $x \ge 1$: $x^2 + 3x - 10 > 0 \Rightarrow (x+5)(x-2) > 0 \Rightarrow x > 2$.
For $x < 1$: $x^2 - 3x - 4 > 0 \Rightarrow (x-4)(x+1) > 0 \Rightarrow x < -1$.
So the inequality fails for $-1 \le x \le 2$: the integers $-1, 0, 1, 2$ — four integers.

questions.question: The graph of $y = \dfrac{1}{a + bx + 4ax^2}$, where $a > 1$, has only one asymptote when
questions.answer: $y = 0$ is always a horizontal asymptote, so there must be no vertical asymptotes: the denominator has no real zeros, $\Delta = b^2 - 16a^2 < 0$, i.e. $-4a < b < 4a$. Since $a > 1$, $4a > 4$, so any $b$ with $-1 \le b \le 4$ satisfies this; A is not guaranteed (e.g. $a = 1.1$, $b = 4.5$).

questions.question:
Use the substitution $u = e^{2x}$ to find
$$\int \left(e^{e^{2x}}\right)^2 e^{2x}\,dx.$$

Three forces $\overrightarrow{F_1}$, $\overrightarrow{F_2}$ and $\overrightarrow{F_3}$ are represented by the vectors $10\mathbf{i} + 20\mathbf{j}$, $20\mathbf{i} - 30\mathbf{j}$ and $-6\mathbf{i} + 20\mathbf{j}$ newtons respectively.

Draw a sketch showing the relative magnitude and direction of the three forces.
questions.answer: All three drawn from the origin on the same axes, to scale: $\overrightarrow{F_1}$ to $(10, 20)$ (first quadrant), $\overrightarrow{F_2}$ to $(20, -30)$ (fourth quadrant, longest), $\overrightarrow{F_3}$ to $(-6, 20)$ (second quadrant).

questions.question:
Three forces $\overrightarrow{F_1}$, $\overrightarrow{F_2}$ and $\overrightarrow{F_3}$ are represented by the vectors $10\mathbf{i} + 20\mathbf{j}$, $20\mathbf{i} - 30\mathbf{j}$ and $-6\mathbf{i} + 20\mathbf{j}$ newtons respectively.

Determine the resultant force, expressed as a vector, and find its magnitude.
questions.answer:
$$\overrightarrow{F} = (10 + 20 - 6)\mathbf{i} + (20 - 30 + 20)\mathbf{j} = 24\mathbf{i} + 10\mathbf{j}$$
$$|\overrightarrow{F}| = \sqrt{24^2 + 10^2} = \sqrt{676} = 26 \text{ N}.$$

questions.question:
Three forces $\overrightarrow{F_1}$, $\overrightarrow{F_2}$ and $\overrightarrow{F_3}$ are represented by the vectors $10\mathbf{i} + 20\mathbf{j}$, $20\mathbf{i} - 30\mathbf{j}$ and $-6\mathbf{i} + 20\mathbf{j}$ newtons respectively. Their resultant is $24\mathbf{i} + 10\mathbf{j}$.

An additional force $\overrightarrow{F_4} = k\mathbf{j}$ is applied so that the resultant of $\overrightarrow{F_1}$, $\overrightarrow{F_2}$, $\overrightarrow{F_3}$ and $\overrightarrow{F_4}$ has magnitude 30 N. What is the value of $k$?
questions.answer:
New resultant $24\mathbf{i} + (10 + k)\mathbf{j}$:
$$24^2 + (k + 10)^2 = 900 \Rightarrow (k + 10)^2 = 324 \Rightarrow k + 10 = \pm 18 \Rightarrow k = 8 \text{ or } k = -28.$$

You are asked to provide an 8-letter password which may only be made up of the letters A, B and C.

If the password must use each of the letters A, B and C at least once, how many possible passwords are there?
questions.answer:
Subtract passwords missing at least one letter (inclusion–exclusion). Passwords missing a given letter: $2^8 = 256$ each (3 letters). Those missing two given letters (all one letter) have been subtracted twice: add back 3.
$$3^8 - 3 \times 2^8 + 3 = 6561 - 768 + 3 = 5796.$$

questions.question:
The quartic polynomial $P(x) = x^4 + px^3 + qx^2 + px + 1$ has $x = \alpha$ as a double zero.

Show that $\alpha^{-1}$ is also a zero of $P(x)$.
questions.answer:
$P(\alpha) = \alpha^4 + p\alpha^3 + q\alpha^2 + p\alpha + 1 = 0$ (note $\alpha \ne 0$ since $P(0) = 1$).
$$P\left(\frac{1}{\alpha}\right) = \frac{1}{\alpha^4} + \frac{p}{\alpha^3} + \frac{q}{\alpha^2} + \frac{p}{\alpha} + 1 = \frac{1 + p\alpha + q\alpha^2 + p\alpha^3 + \alpha^4}{\alpha^4} = \frac{P(\alpha)}{\alpha^4} = 0.$$
So $\frac{1}{\alpha}$ is a zero.

questions.question:
The quartic polynomial $P(x) = x^4 + px^3 + qx^2 + px + 1$ has $x = \alpha$ as a double zero. Also, $\alpha^{-1}$ is a zero of $P(x)$.

Find the fourth root in terms of $\alpha$.
questions.answer:
The roots are $\alpha, \alpha, \frac{1}{\alpha}, \beta$. Product of roots $= \frac{e}{a} = 1$:
$$\alpha^2 \cdot \frac{1}{\alpha} \cdot \beta = 1 \Rightarrow \beta = \frac{1}{\alpha}.$$
(So $\frac{1}{\alpha}$ is also a double root.)

questions.question:
The quartic polynomial $P(x) = x^4 + px^3 + qx^2 + px + 1$ has $x = \alpha$ as a double zero. Its roots are $\alpha, \alpha, \frac{1}{\alpha}, \frac{1}{\alpha}$.

Show that $p^2 = 4(q - 2)$.
questions.answer:
Sum of roots: $2\alpha + \frac{2}{\alpha} = -p$, so $p^2 = 4\left(\alpha + \frac{1}{\alpha}\right)^2 = 4\left(\alpha^2 + \frac{1}{\alpha^2} + 2\right)$.

Sum of products two at a time: $\alpha\cdot\alpha + 4\left(\alpha\cdot\frac{1}{\alpha}\right) + \frac{1}{\alpha}\cdot\frac{1}{\alpha} = q$, so $q = \alpha^2 + \frac{1}{\alpha^2} + 4$, i.e. $\alpha^2 + \frac{1}{\alpha^2} + 2 = q - 2$.

Hence $p^2 = 4(q - 2)$.

questions.question:
Show that the differential equation
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2xy}{x^2 - 1}$$
describes a family of parabolas with $x$-intercepts at $(1, 0)$ and $(-1, 0)$.
questions.answer:
Separate variables:
$$\int \frac{dy}{y} = \int \frac{2x}{x^2 - 1}\,dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| = \ln|x^2 - 1| + c \Rightarrow y = A(x^2 - 1) = A(x - 1)(x + 1),$$
where $A = \pm e^c$ (and $A = 0$ also satisfies the equation). This is a family of parabolas with $x$-intercepts $(1, 0)$ and $(-1, 0)$.

questions.question:
Consider the differential equation
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{1 - x^2}{2xy}.$$
Find the equation of the curve which satisfies this differential equation and passes through the point $(1, 1)$. Express your answer as a function of $x$.
questions.answer:
$$\int 2y\,dy = \int \left(\frac{1}{x} - x\right)dx \Rightarrow y^2 = \ln|x| - \frac{x^2}{2} + C.$$
At $(1, 1)$: $1 = 0 - \frac{1}{2} + C$, so $C = \frac{3}{2}$. Since $y = 1 > 0$ at $x = 1$, take the positive root:
$$y = \sqrt{\ln x - \frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{3}{2}}.$$

questions.question: The differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2xy}{x^2 - 1}$ describes a family of parabolas $y = A(x^2 - 1)$. The curve $y = \sqrt{\ln x - \frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{3}{2}}$ satisfies $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 - x^2}{2xy}$. What can be said about this curve in relation to the family of parabolas?
questions.answer:
At any point $(x, y)$, the product of the two gradients is
$$\frac{2xy}{x^2 - 1} \times \frac{1 - x^2}{2xy} = -1,$$
so the curve meets every parabola of the family at right angles (it is an orthogonal trajectory).

questions.question: Solve for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$: $\sin x + \cos 2x - \sin 3x = 0$.
questions.answer:
Using $\sin 3x = 3\sin x - 4\sin^3 x$:
$$\sin x - \sin 3x = -2\sin x + 4\sin^3 x = -2\sin x(1 - 2\sin^2 x) = -2\sin x\cos 2x.$$
So the equation becomes $\cos 2x - 2\sin x\cos 2x = 0$, i.e. $\cos 2x(1 - 2\sin x) = 0$.

- $\cos 2x = 0$: $2x = (2k+1)\frac{\pi}{2}$, so $x = (2k+1)\frac{\pi}{4}$.
- $\sin x = \frac{1}{2}$: $x = k\pi + (-1)^k\frac{\pi}{6}$,

where $k \in \mathbb{Z}$.

questions.question: Sketch the graph of the curve $y = 3\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$.
questions.answer: Domain $-2 \le x \le 2$, range $0 \le y \le 3\pi$. The curve is decreasing, from $(-2, 3\pi)$ through $\left(0, \frac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ (point of symmetry, where it is steepest, not a horizontal inflection) to $(2, 0)$. It has vertical tangents at the endpoints.

questions.question: The region bounded by the curve $y = 3\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$, the $y$-axis and the lines $y = \frac{\pi}{2}$ and $y = \frac{5\pi}{2}$ is rotated around the $y$-axis to form an hourglass. Find the volume of the hourglass formed.
questions.answer:
$x = 2\cos\frac{y}{3}$, so $x^2 = 4\cos^2\frac{y}{3} = 2\left(1 + \cos\frac{2y}{3}\right)$.
$$V = \pi\int_{\pi/2}^{5\pi/2} x^2\,dy = 2\pi\left[y + \frac{3}{2}\sin\frac{2y}{3}\right]_{\pi/2}^{5\pi/2} = 2\pi\left[2\pi + \frac{3}{2}\left(\sin\frac{5\pi}{3} - \sin\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right]$$
$$= 2\pi\left(2\pi - \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 4\pi^2 - 3\sqrt{3}\pi = 4\pi\left(\pi - \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}\right) \text{ units}^3.$$

questions.question:
Prove by mathematical induction that for all positive integers $n \ge 1$,
$$1^2 \times 2 + 2^2 \times 2^2 + 3^2 \times 2^3 + \dots + n^2 \times 2^n = (n^2 - 2n + 3)2^{n+1} - 6.$$
questions.answer:
**$n = 1$:** LHS $= 1 \times 2 = 2$; RHS $= (1 - 2 + 3)2^2 - 6 = 2$. True.

**Assume true for $n = k$:** $1^2 \times 2 + \dots + k^2 \times 2^k = (k^2 - 2k + 3)2^{k+1} - 6$.

**Prove for $n = k+1$:** RHS required $= ((k+1)^2 - 2(k+1) + 3)2^{k+2} - 6 = (k^2 + 2)2^{k+2} - 6$.
$$\text{LHS} = (k^2 - 2k + 3)2^{k+1} - 6 + (k+1)^2 2^{k+1} \quad \text{(by the assumption)}$$
$$= 2^{k+1}(k^2 - 2k + 3 + k^2 + 2k + 1) - 6 = 2^{k+1}(2k^2 + 4) - 6 = (k^2 + 2)2^{k+2} - 6 = \text{RHS}.$$
Hence true for all integers $n \ge 1$ by mathematical induction.

questions.question:
Let $f(x) = \frac{1}{2}(2x - 1 + 2\sin x)$. The graphs of $y = f(x)$ and $y = f^{-1}(x)$ are shown.

Find the points of intersection of the two curves.
questions.answer:
Since $f$ is increasing, the curves meet on $y = x$: $\frac{1}{2}(2x - 1 + 2\sin x) = x \Rightarrow \sin x = \frac{1}{2}$.
From the graph, $x = \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{5\pi}{6}, \frac{13\pi}{6}$: the points $\left(\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{6}\right)$, $\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}, \frac{5\pi}{6}\right)$, $\left(\frac{13\pi}{6}, \frac{13\pi}{6}\right)$.

questions.question:
Let $f(x) = \frac{1}{2}(2x - 1 + 2\sin x)$. The graphs of $y = f(x)$ and $y = f^{-1}(x)$ are shown. They intersect at $x = \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{5\pi}{6}, \frac{13\pi}{6}$ (on the line $y = x$).

Find the shaded area enclosed by the two curves.
questions.answer:
By symmetry in $y = x$, the area is twice the area between $y = f(x)$ and $y = x$. Note $f(x) - x = \sin x - \frac{1}{2}$.
$$A = 2\left[\int_{\pi/6}^{5\pi/6}\left(\sin x - \tfrac{1}{2}\right)dx + \int_{5\pi/6}^{13\pi/6}\left(\tfrac{1}{2} - \sin x\right)dx\right]$$
$$= 2\left(\left[-\cos x - \tfrac{x}{2}\right]_{\pi/6}^{5\pi/6} + \left[\tfrac{x}{2} + \cos x\right]_{5\pi/6}^{13\pi/6}\right) = 2\left[\left(\sqrt{3} - \frac{\pi}{3}\right) + \left(\sqrt{3} + \frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right] = 4\sqrt{3} + \frac{2\pi}{3}.$$

questions.question: Six points $P_1, \dots, P_6$ form the vertices of a regular hexagon $H_1$. An animated program moves these six points at a constant speed of 3 cm/s around the perimeter of another regular hexagon, $H_2$, which has side length 20 cm (as shown). Initially, the six vertices of $H_1$ lie on top of the six vertices of $H_2$. Determine the rate of change of the area of $H_1$ ten seconds after the animation begins.
questions.answer:
Let $x$ be the distance each point has moved along its side of $H_2$ (for $0 \le x \le 20$), so $\frac{dx}{dt} = 3$. The side $\ell$ of $H_1$ joins points $x$ and $20 - x$ from a vertex of $H_2$, with interior angle $120°$:
$$\ell^2 = x^2 + (20 - x)^2 - 2x(20 - x)\cos 120° = x^2 - 20x + 400.$$
Area of $H_1$: $A = 6 \times \frac{1}{2}\ell^2\sin 60° = \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}(x^2 - 20x + 400)$.
$$\frac{dA}{dt} = \frac{dA}{dx}\cdot\frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}(2x - 20) \times 3 = 9\sqrt{3}(x - 10).$$
After 10 s each point has moved 30 cm, i.e. 10 cm past the next vertex, so $x = 10$ and $\frac{dA}{dt} = 0$ cm²/s (the area is at its minimum).

questions.question: Triangle $OAB$ is defined by two non-parallel, non-zero vectors $\overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{OB} = \mathbf{b}$. The angle between $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ is $\theta$. Express the area of triangle $OAB$ in terms of dot products of $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$.
questions.answer:
$\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b} = |\mathbf{a}||\mathbf{b}|\cos\theta$ and $2A = |\mathbf{a}||\mathbf{b}|\sin\theta$. Squaring and adding:
$$(\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b})^2 + 4A^2 = |\mathbf{a}|^2|\mathbf{b}|^2(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta) = |\mathbf{a}|^2|\mathbf{b}|^2.$$
Since $A > 0$ and $|\mathbf{a}|^2 = \mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{a}$:
$$A = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{(\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{a})(\mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{b}) - (\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b})^2}.$$

questions.question:
Show that
$$\cos\left(\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\right) + \cos^{-1}x\right) = 0$$
for all real $x$, $-1 < x < 1$. You may assume that the range of $\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}$ is all real numbers.
questions.answer:
Let $\alpha = \tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}$, so $\tan\alpha = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}$ with $-\frac{\pi}{2} < \alpha < \frac{\pi}{2}$, and $\alpha$ has the same sign as $x$. Then $\cos\alpha > 0$ and
$$\cos\alpha = \sqrt{1 - x^2}, \qquad \sin\alpha = x$$
(check: $\sin^2\alpha + \cos^2\alpha = 1$ and the ratio is $\tan\alpha$; this holds for $x$ positive, negative or zero).

Let $\beta = \cos^{-1}x \in (0, \pi)$, so $\cos\beta = x$ and $\sin\beta = \sqrt{1 - x^2}$ (as $\sin\beta > 0$).
$$\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta = \sqrt{1 - x^2}\cdot x - x\sqrt{1 - x^2} = 0.$$

questions.question: A plane experiences two forces: 10 N of gravity straight down, and 60 N of thrust at an angle of 15° above the horizontal. What is the magnitude of the net force, to the nearest newton?
questions.answer: $\mathbf{F} = 60\cos 15°\,\mathbf{i} + (60\sin 15° - 10)\mathbf{j} = 57.96\mathbf{i} + 5.53\mathbf{j}$, so $|\mathbf{F}| = \sqrt{57.96^2 + 5.53^2} \approx 58$ N.

questions.question: Suppose $a, b, c$ form a Pythagorean triple where $a < b < c$. What is the maximum value the function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{a\sin x + b\cos x + 2c}$ can attain?
questions.answer: $a\sin x + b\cos x = R\sin(x + \alpha)$ with $R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2} = c$, so it ranges over $[-c, c]$. The denominator is at least $2c - c = c > 0$, so the maximum of $f$ is $\dfrac{1}{c}$.

questions.question: Find an expression for the number of ways all the letters of the word EPSILON can be arranged such that the three vowels are all next to each other.
questions.answer: Treat the vowels E, I, O as one block: arrange the block and P, S, L, N in $5!$ ways, and the vowels within the block in $3!$ ways: $3! \times 5!$.

questions.question:
Two vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ have $|\mathbf{a}| = 3$ and $|\mathbf{b}| = 5$, and the angle between them is $120°$ (as shown). Let $\mathbf{c}$ be the vector such that $\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c} = \mathbf{0}$.

Find $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}$.
questions.answer: $$\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b} = |\mathbf{a}||\mathbf{b}|\cos 120° = 3 \times 5 \times \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = -\frac{15}{2}.$$

questions.question:
Two vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ have $|\mathbf{a}| = 3$ and $|\mathbf{b}| = 5$, and the angle between them is $120°$ (as shown). Let $\mathbf{c}$ be the vector such that $\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b} + \mathbf{c} = \mathbf{0}$. Also $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b} = -\frac{15}{2}$.

Expand and evaluate $(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b})\cdot(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b})$.
questions.answer: $$(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b})\cdot(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b}) = \mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{a} + 2\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b} + \mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{b} = |\mathbf{a}|^2 + 2\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b} + |\mathbf{b}|^2 = 9 - 15 + 25 = 19.$$

questions.answer:
$\mathbf{c} = -(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b})$, so $|\mathbf{c}|^2 = (\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b})\cdot(\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b}) = 19$ and $|\mathbf{c}| = \sqrt{19}$.

(Alternatively, $\mathbf{a}$, $\mathbf{b}$, $\mathbf{c}$ placed head to tail form a triangle with an angle of $60°$ between sides 3 and 5: $|\mathbf{c}|^2 = 9 + 25 - 2(3)(5)\cos 60° = 19$.)

questions.question:
Prove by mathematical induction that, for all integers $n \ge 1$,
$$\frac{2}{1\times 3} + \frac{2}{2\times 4} + \frac{2}{3\times 5} + \dots + \frac{2}{n(n+2)} = \frac{3}{2} - \frac{2n + 3}{(n+1)(n+2)}.$$
questions.answer:
**$n = 1$:** LHS $= \frac{2}{3}$; RHS $= \frac{3}{2} - \frac{5}{6} = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$. True.

**Assume true for $n = k$:** $\frac{2}{1\times3} + \dots + \frac{2}{k(k+2)} = \frac{3}{2} - \frac{2k+3}{(k+1)(k+2)}$.

**Prove for $n = k + 1$:** required RHS $= \frac{3}{2} - \frac{2k+5}{(k+2)(k+3)}$.
$$\text{LHS} = \frac{3}{2} - \frac{2k+3}{(k+1)(k+2)} + \frac{2}{(k+1)(k+3)} = \frac{3}{2} - \frac{(2k+3)(k+3) - 2(k+2)}{(k+1)(k+2)(k+3)}$$
$$= \frac{3}{2} - \frac{2k^2 + 7k + 5}{(k+1)(k+2)(k+3)} = \frac{3}{2} - \frac{(2k+5)(k+1)}{(k+1)(k+2)(k+3)} = \frac{3}{2} - \frac{2k+5}{(k+2)(k+3)}.$$
So true for $n = k + 1$ if true for $n = k$. Hence true for all integers $n \ge 1$ by mathematical induction.

questions.question: Three distinct non-zero vectors are given by $\overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a}$, $\overrightarrow{OB} = \mathbf{b}$ and $\overrightarrow{OC} = \mathbf{c}$. If $\overrightarrow{OA}$ is perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{BC}$ and $\overrightarrow{OB}$ is perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{CA}$, show that $\overrightarrow{OC}$ is perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{AB}$.
questions.answer:
$\overrightarrow{OA} \perp \overrightarrow{BC}$: $\mathbf{a}\cdot(\mathbf{c} - \mathbf{b}) = 0$, so $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{c}$. (1)

$\overrightarrow{OB} \perp \overrightarrow{CA}$: $\mathbf{b}\cdot(\mathbf{a} - \mathbf{c}) = 0$, so $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{c}$. (2)

From (1) and (2), $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{c} = \mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{c}$, so $\mathbf{c}\cdot(\mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a}) = 0$. Since $\mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a} = \overrightarrow{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{OC}$ is perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{AB}$.

questions.question: Show that $\tan\dfrac{\pi}{12} = 2 - \sqrt{3}$.
questions.answer:
$$\tan\frac{\pi}{12} = \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3} - \frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{1 + \sqrt{3}} \times \frac{1 - \sqrt{3}}{1 - \sqrt{3}} = \frac{\sqrt{3} - 3 - 1 + \sqrt{3}}{1 - 3} = \frac{-4 + 2\sqrt{3}}{-2} = 2 - \sqrt{3}.$$
(Alternatively, use $\tan\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{2t}{1 - t^2}$ with $t = \tan\frac{\pi}{12}$, solve $t^2 + 2\sqrt{3}t - 1 = 0$ and take the positive root since $\frac{\pi}{12}$ is in the first quadrant.)

questions.question: Given that $\sin(x + \alpha) = k\cos(x - \alpha)$, show that $\tan x = \dfrac{k - \tan\alpha}{1 - k\tan\alpha}$.
questions.answer:
$$\sin x\cos\alpha + \cos x\sin\alpha = k\cos x\cos\alpha + k\sin x\sin\alpha.$$
Divide by $\cos x\cos\alpha$: $\tan x + \tan\alpha = k + k\tan x\tan\alpha$, so $\tan x(1 - k\tan\alpha) = k - \tan\alpha$ and
$$\tan x = \frac{k - \tan\alpha}{1 - k\tan\alpha}.$$

questions.question:
It is known that $\tan\dfrac{\pi}{12} = 2 - \sqrt{3}$, and that if $\sin(x + \alpha) = k\cos(x - \alpha)$ then $\tan x = \dfrac{k - \tan\alpha}{1 - k\tan\alpha}$. Using these results, solve, for $0 < x < 2\pi$, the equation
$$(\sqrt{3} - 1)\sin\left(x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \cos\left(x - \frac{\pi}{3}\right).$$
questions.answer:
Here $\alpha = \frac{\pi}{3}$ and $k = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3} - 1}$:
$$\tan x = \frac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{3} - 1} - \sqrt{3}}{1 - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3} - 1}} = \frac{1 - \sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3} - 1)}{\sqrt{3} - 1 - \sqrt{3}} = \frac{1 - 3 + \sqrt{3}}{-1} = 2 - \sqrt{3} = \tan\frac{\pi}{12}.$$
So $x = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$ or $x = \dfrac{13\pi}{12}$.

A four-metre-long water tank, open at the top, is in the shape of a triangular prism. The triangular face is a right isosceles triangle with congruent sides of length 1 m, with the right angle at the bottom (as shown). Initially the tank is completely full of water, but it develops a leak and loses water at a constant rate of 0.08 cubic metres per hour. Let $h$ be the depth of water, in metres, in the tank after $t$ hours.

Show that the volume, $V$, of water in the tank in cubic metres is given by $V = 4h^2$.
questions.answer:
The water's cross-section is a right isosceles triangle similar to the end face, with its right angle at the bottom. Its height (depth) is $h$ and the angle between each sloping side and the vertical is $45°$, so the width of the water surface is $2h$.
Cross-sectional area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 2h \times h = h^2$, so $V = 4h^2$.

questions.question:
A four-metre-long water tank, open at the top, is in the shape of a triangular prism. The triangular face is a right isosceles triangle with congruent sides of length 1 m, with the right angle at the bottom (as shown). Initially the tank is completely full of water, but it develops a leak and loses water at a constant rate of 0.08 cubic metres per hour. Let $h$ be the depth of water, in metres, in the tank after $t$ hours. The volume of water is $V = 4h^2$.

Determine the rate of change of the depth when the depth is 0.6 metres.
questions.answer:
$\frac{dV}{dt} = -0.08$ and $\frac{dV}{dh} = 8h$.
$$\frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dt} \div \frac{dV}{dh} = \frac{-0.08}{8 \times 0.6} = -\frac{1}{60} \text{ m/h}.$$
The depth is decreasing at $\frac{1}{60}$ m per hour.

questions.question: The diagram shows the graph of $y = f(x)$, where $f(x) = \dfrac{4x + 4}{x + 2}$, $x > -2$. Sketch the graph of $y = |f(x)|$, showing clearly the intercepts on the axes and the equations of any asymptotes.
questions.answer:
$f(x) = 4 - \dfrac{4}{x + 2}$, with $x$-intercept $-1$ and $y$-intercept 2.

For $x \ge -1$, $y = |f(x)|$ is the same as $y = f(x)$: rising from $(-1, 0)$ through $(0, 2)$ towards the asymptote $y = 4$. For $-2 < x < -1$, the part below the axis is reflected above it, rising to $+\infty$ as $x \to -2^+$ (vertical asymptote $x = -2$). There is a sharp point (cusp) at $(-1, 0)$.

questions.question: Find $\displaystyle\int 3x^2\left(x^3 - 1\right)^4 dx$ using the substitution $u = x^3 - 1$.
Consider the expansion of $\left(\dfrac{x^3}{2} + \dfrac{a}{x}\right)^8$. If the constant term is 5103, determine the possible value(s) of $a$.
questions.answer:
General term: $\binom{8}{r}\left(\frac{x^3}{2}\right)^{8-r}\left(\frac{a}{x}\right)^r = \binom{8}{r}2^{-(8-r)}a^r x^{3(8-r) - r}$.
Constant term: $24 - 4r = 0 \Rightarrow r = 6$:
$$\binom{8}{6}2^{-2}a^6 = 7a^6 = 5103 \Rightarrow a^6 = 729 \Rightarrow a = \pm 3.$$

questions.question: Find $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\cos^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}(-x)\right)$.
Given that $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\cos^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}(-x)\right) = 0$, prove that $\cos^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}(-x) = \pi$.
questions.answer:
Since the derivative is 0 on $(-1, 1)$, $\cos^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}(-x) = C$ there. At $x = 0$: $\frac{\pi}{2} + \frac{\pi}{2} = \pi$, so $C = \pi$.
At the endpoints: $\cos^{-1}(1) + \cos^{-1}(-1) = 0 + \pi = \pi$ and $\cos^{-1}(-1) + \cos^{-1}(1) = \pi$.
Hence $\cos^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}(-x) = \pi$ for all $x \in [-1, 1]$.

questions.question:
A liquid is being heated in an oven maintained at a constant temperature of 180°C. The rate of increase of the temperature of the liquid at any time $t$ minutes is proportional to $180 - \theta$, where $\theta$°C is the temperature of the liquid at that time.

Write a differential equation connecting $\theta$ and $t$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{d\theta}{dt} = k(180 - \theta)$, where $k > 0$ is a constant.

questions.question:
A liquid is being heated in an oven maintained at a constant temperature of 180°C. The rate of increase of the temperature of the liquid at any time $t$ minutes is proportional to $180 - \theta$, where $\theta$°C is the temperature of the liquid at that time. So $\frac{d\theta}{dt} = k(180 - \theta)$.

When the liquid was placed in the oven its temperature was 25°C, and 5 minutes later its temperature had risen to 75°C. Find the temperature of the liquid after another 5 minutes.
questions.answer:
Separate variables: $\displaystyle\int \frac{d\theta}{180 - \theta} = \int k\,dt \Rightarrow -\ln(180 - \theta) = kt + c$.
At $t = 0$, $\theta = 25$: $c = -\ln 155$, so $\ln\dfrac{155}{180 - \theta} = kt$.
At $t = 5$, $\theta = 75$: $5k = \ln\dfrac{155}{105} = \ln\dfrac{31}{21}$.
At $t = 10$: $\ln\dfrac{155}{180 - \theta} = 2\ln\dfrac{31}{21}$, so
$$180 - \theta = 155\left(\frac{21}{31}\right)^2 = \frac{2205}{31} \Rightarrow \theta = \frac{3375}{31} \approx 109°\text{C}.$$

Solve for the $x$-coordinates at which the two curves intersect.
questions.answer: On the $x$-axis: $9\pi^2 - 16x^2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \pm\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$. Check: $-1 + 2\sin^2\frac{3\pi}{4} = -1 + 2\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 0$ ✓.

questions.question:
The design for a company logo is shown. The upper border of the logo is part of the curve $y = \dfrac{9\pi^2 - 16x^2}{32}$, while the lower border is part of the curve $y = -1 + 2\sin^2 x$. The curves intersect on the $x$-axis. They intersect at $x = \pm\frac{3\pi}{4}$.

Determine the area of the company logo correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer:
Note $-1 + 2\sin^2 x = -\cos 2x$.
$$A = \int_{-3\pi/4}^{3\pi/4}\left(\frac{9\pi^2 - 16x^2}{32} + \cos 2x\right)dx = 2\left[\frac{9\pi^2x}{32} - \frac{x^3}{6} + \frac{\sin 2x}{2}\right]_0^{3\pi/4}$$
$$= 2\left(\frac{27\pi^3}{128} - \frac{9\pi^3}{128} - \frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{9\pi^3}{32} - 1 \approx 7.72 \text{ units}^2.$$

questions.question:
The diagram shows the vertical cross-section through the centre of a goldfish bowl. The glass part of the bowl sits on a solid base (shaded). Each horizontal cross-section is a circle. The vertical cross-section through the centre of the bowl is symmetrical about the $y$-axis and can be described by the equation
$$\frac{x^2}{64} + \frac{(y - 5)^2}{16} = 1.$$
The dashed horizontal line represents the diameter of the open top of the bowl. Given that the open top has a diameter of 15 cm, and that this is above the diameter of the bowl at its widest point, find the capacity of the glass part of the bowl, assuming that the thickness of the glass may be regarded as negligible.
questions.answer:
The bowl's bottom is the lowest point of the ellipse, $y = 1$. At the top, $x = 7.5$:
$$(y - 5)^2 = 16\left(1 - \frac{56.25}{64}\right) = \frac{31}{16} \Rightarrow y = 5 + \frac{\sqrt{31}}{4} \text{ (above the widest point, } y = 5\text{)}.$$
With $x^2 = 64 - 4(y - 5)^2$ and $u = y - 5$:
$$V = \pi\int_{-4}^{\sqrt{31}/4}\left(64 - 4u^2\right)du = \pi\left[64u - \frac{4u^3}{3}\right]_{-4}^{\sqrt{31}/4} = \pi\left(16\sqrt{31} - \frac{31\sqrt{31}}{48} + 256 - \frac{256}{3}\right)$$
$$= \pi\left(\frac{737\sqrt{31}}{48} + \frac{512}{3}\right) \approx 805 \text{ cm}^3.$$
(No solution was provided for this question; this working is our own.)

questions.question: Find $\displaystyle\int_0^2 2x\sqrt{1-\frac x2}\,dx$ using the substitution $u=1-\dfrac x2$.

questions.question: Two rows of square tiles each have 10 tiles. 4 tiles in the top row and 6 in the bottom row are to be shaded so that exactly two shaded tiles in the top row are directly above a shaded tile in the bottom row. In how many ways can this be done?
questions.answer:
Choose the 4 top tiles: $\dbinom{10}4$. Choose which 2 of them have a shaded tile below: $\dbinom42$. The other 4 shaded bottom tiles go in the 6 columns with no shaded top tile: $\dbinom64$.

$$\binom{10}4\binom42\binom64=18\,900$$

questions.question: $\sqrt6\sin x+\sqrt2\cos x$ can be written as $R\sin(x+\alpha)$, with $R>0$ and $0<\alpha<\dfrac\pi2$. Using this or otherwise, solve $\sqrt6\sin x+\sqrt2\cos x=2$ for $x\in[0,2\pi]$.
questions.answer:
$R=\sqrt8$ and $\tan\alpha=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt6}$, so $\alpha=\dfrac\pi6$.

$\sqrt8\sin\left(x+\dfrac\pi6\right)=2$ gives $x+\dfrac\pi6=\dfrac\pi4,\dfrac{3\pi}4$, so $x=\dfrac\pi{12},\ \dfrac{7\pi}{12}$.

questions.question: Use mathematical induction to prove that $9^n-4^n$ is divisible by 5 for all integers $n\ge1$.
questions.answer:
**$n=1$:** $9-4=5$, divisible by 5.

**Assume** $9^k-4^k=5p$ for an integer $p$.

**$n=k+1$:** $9^{k+1}-4^{k+1}=9(9^k-4^k)+5\cdot4^k=5(9p+4^k)$, divisible by 5.

Hence by induction the result holds for all $n\ge1$.

questions.question: Given $\underset{\sim}{u}=2\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}$ and $\underset{\sim}{v}=-2\underset{\sim}{i}+4\underset{\sim}{j}$, find $\text{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{u}}\underset{\sim}{v}$.
questions.answer: $$\text{proj}_{\underset{\sim}{u}}\underset{\sim}{v}=\frac{\underset{\sim}{v}\cdot\underset{\sim}{u}}{\underset{\sim}{u}\cdot\underset{\sim}{u}}\underset{\sim}{u}=\frac8{13}\left(2\underset{\sim}{i}+3\underset{\sim}{j}\right)$$

questions.question: Prove that $\tan4\theta-\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin3\theta}{\cos4\theta\cos\theta}$.

questions.question: Given $\tan4\theta-\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin3\theta}{\cos4\theta\cos\theta}$, solve $\tan4\theta=\tan\theta$ for $0\le\theta\le\pi$.

We need $\sin3\theta=0$ (with $\cos4\theta\cos\theta\ne0$): $3\theta=0,\pi,2\pi,3\pi$.

$$\theta=0,\ \frac\pi3,\ \frac{2\pi}3,\ \pi$$

prev.answer: $$\tan4\theta-\tan\theta=\frac{\sin4\theta\cos\theta-\cos4\theta\sin\theta}{\cos4\theta\cos\theta}=\frac{\sin(4\theta-\theta)}{\cos4\theta\cos\theta}=\frac{\sin3\theta}{\cos4\theta\cos\theta}$$

questions.question: Triangle $ABC$ has vertices with position vectors $\underset{\sim}{a},\underset{\sim}{b},\underset{\sim}{c}$. $D$ lies on $BC$ with $BD=\frac13BC$, $X$ lies on $AC$ with $AX=\frac14AC$, and $M$ is the midpoint of $AD$. Express $\overrightarrow{AM}$ in terms of $\underset{\sim}{a},\underset{\sim}{b},\underset{\sim}{c}$.
questions.answer:
$\overrightarrow{AD}=\overrightarrow{AB}+\tfrac13\overrightarrow{BC}=(\underset{\sim}{b}-\underset{\sim}{a})+\tfrac13(\underset{\sim}{c}-\underset{\sim}{b})=-\underset{\sim}{a}+\tfrac23\underset{\sim}{b}+\tfrac13\underset{\sim}{c}$

$$\overrightarrow{AM}=\tfrac12\overrightarrow{AD}=-\tfrac12\underset{\sim}{a}+\tfrac13\underset{\sim}{b}+\tfrac16\underset{\sim}{c}$$

questions.question: Triangle $ABC$ has vertices with position vectors $\underset{\sim}{a},\underset{\sim}{b},\underset{\sim}{c}$. $D$ lies on $BC$ with $BD=\frac13BC$, $X$ lies on $AC$ with $AX=\frac14AC$, and $M$ is the midpoint of $AD$. Given $\overrightarrow{AM}=-\frac12\underset{\sim}{a}+\frac13\underset{\sim}{b}+\frac16\underset{\sim}{c}$, show that $B$, $M$ and $X$ are collinear and hence find $BM:MX$.
questions.answer:
$\overrightarrow{BM}=\overrightarrow{BA}+\overrightarrow{AM}=\tfrac12\underset{\sim}{a}-\tfrac23\underset{\sim}{b}+\tfrac16\underset{\sim}{c}$

$\overrightarrow{MX}=\overrightarrow{AX}-\overrightarrow{AM}=\tfrac14(\underset{\sim}{c}-\underset{\sim}{a})-\overrightarrow{AM}=\tfrac14\underset{\sim}{a}-\tfrac13\underset{\sim}{b}+\tfrac1{12}\underset{\sim}{c}$

So $\overrightarrow{MX}=\tfrac12\overrightarrow{BM}$. The vectors are parallel with the common point $M$, so $B,M,X$ are collinear and $BM:MX=2:1$.

questions.question: After $t$ years from the start of 2021 the population is $N=70+Ae^{0.1t}$, where $A>0$. Show that $\dfrac{dN}{dt}=0.1(N-70)$.
After $t$ years from the start of 2021 the population is $N=70+Ae^{0.1t}$, where $A>0$. There were 100 people at the start of 2021. Find the year in which the population size will exceed 190.
questions.answer:
$A=30$. $190=70+30e^{0.1t}$ gives $e^{0.1t}=4$, $t=10\ln4\approx13.86$.

The population exceeds 190 during **2034**.

questions.question: Show that the normal to $y=\sin^{-1}\left(x+\dfrac\pi2\right)+\dfrac\pi2$ at the point where $x=-\dfrac\pi2$ passes through the origin.
questions.answer:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac1{\sqrt{1-(x+\pi/2)^2}}=1$ at $x=-\dfrac\pi2$, where $y=\dfrac\pi2$.

The normal has gradient $-1$: $y-\dfrac\pi2=-\left(x+\dfrac\pi2\right)$, that is $y=-x$, which passes through the origin.

questions.question: A student kicks a football from ground level at angle $\theta$ and speed $V$ m/s. After $t$ seconds its displacement is $\underset{\sim}{r}(t)=(Vt\cos\theta)\underset{\sim}{i}+(Vt\sin\theta-5t^2)\underset{\sim}{j}$. Two seconds after being kicked, the ball just clears the far side of a 5 m high building. The building is 5 m wide and its closest wall is 10 m from the student. $d_1$ is the distance by which the ball clears the closest wall, and $d_2$ is the distance from the far wall to the point of impact. Show that $d_2-d_1<1$.

500 fish are released into a lake with carrying capacity 10 000. The population $N$ after $t$ years satisfies $\dfrac{dN}{dt}=kN(10\,000-N)$, where $k$ is a constant. Given $\dfrac{10\,000}{N(10\,000-N)}=\dfrac1N+\dfrac1{10\,000-N}$, show that $N=\dfrac{10\,000}{1+19e^{-10\,000kt}}$.
A fish population is $N=\dfrac{10\,000}{1+19e^{-10\,000kt}}$ after $t$ years, with $k=\dfrac1{10\,000}\ln\dfrac{57}{17}$. Find, to the nearest month, how long it takes the population to reach 7000.
questions.answer:
$1+19e^{-10\,000kt}=\dfrac{10}7$ gives $e^{-10\,000kt}=\dfrac3{133}$.

$$t=\frac{\ln(133/3)}{\ln(57/17)}\approx3.134\text{ years}\approx38\text{ months}$$

questions.question: $X$ is a random variable such that $X \sim \text{Bin}(30, 0.4)$. Which of the following gives $E(X)$ and $\text{Var}(X)$?
Which of the following is the range of $\tan^{-1}(\sin x)$?
questions.answer: $\sin x$ takes all values in $[-1, 1]$ and $\tan^{-1}$ is increasing, so the range is $[\tan^{-1}(-1), \tan^{-1}1] = \left[-\frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{4}\right]$.

questions.question: Which of the following gives the number of values of $x$ in the interval $[0, 5\pi]$ that satisfy the equation $3\sin^2 x - 7\sin x + 2 = 0$?
questions.answer: $(3\sin x - 1)(\sin x - 2) = 0$, and $\sin x = 2$ is impossible, so $\sin x = \frac{1}{3}$. This has 2 solutions in each of $[0, 2\pi]$ and $[2\pi, 4\pi]$, and 2 more in $[4\pi, 5\pi]$ (where $\sin x \ge 0$): 6 solutions.

questions.question: Let $f(x) = x^3$ where $x \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$. Which of the following is the domain of $f^{-1}(x)$?
questions.answer: The domain of $f^{-1}$ is the range of $f$: $\{0, 1, 8, 27\}$.

In the diagram, $AOB$ is a diameter of the circle $ABC$ with centre $O$. Point $C$ lies on the circumference of the circle. If $\overrightarrow{OC} = \mathbf{r}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC} = \mathbf{s}$, to which of the following is $\overrightarrow{AC}$ equal?
questions.answer:
$\overrightarrow{OB} = \overrightarrow{OC} + \overrightarrow{CB} = \mathbf{r} - \mathbf{s}$, so $\overrightarrow{OA} = -\overrightarrow{OB} = \mathbf{s} - \mathbf{r}$.
$\overrightarrow{AC} = \overrightarrow{OC} - \overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{r} - (\mathbf{s} - \mathbf{r}) = 2\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{s}$.

questions.question: Which of the following is the unit vector perpendicular to $\mathbf{p} = -6\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j}$?
questions.answer:
$(-6)(1) + (2)(3) = 0$, and $\left|\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\mathbf{i} + \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\mathbf{j}\right| = 1$. So B is a unit vector perpendicular to $\mathbf{p}$.

Note: the paper's answer key gives C, but $(-6)(1) + (2)(-3) = -12 \ne 0$, so C is not perpendicular to $\mathbf{p}$.

questions.question: Which of the following differential equations could represent the slope field shown?
questions.answer: The slopes are zero on the $y$-axis, vertical on the $x$-axis, positive everywhere above the $x$-axis and negative everywhere below it (the same on both sides of the $y$-axis). So the sign depends only on $y$: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^2}{y}$.

questions.question: There are 11 points in a plane such that 4 of the points are collinear (and no other three are collinear). Which of the following gives the number of lines that may be formed such that those lines pass through at least two of the 11 points?
questions.answer: $\binom{11}{2} = 55$ pairs, but the $\binom{4}{2} = 6$ pairs from the collinear points all give the same line: $55 - 6 + 1 = 50$.

questions.question: For the binomial expansion of $(2 + kx)^7$, where $k > 0$ is a constant, it is given that the coefficient of $x^2$ is six times the coefficient of $x$. Which of the following is the value of $k$?
questions.answer: Coefficient of $x^2$: $\binom{7}{2}2^5k^2 = 672k^2$. Coefficient of $x$: $\binom{7}{1}2^6k = 448k$. $672k^2 = 6 \times 448k \Rightarrow k = 4$.

questions.question: Given $\mathbf{a} = 3\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{b} = -2\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j}$, find $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}$.
questions.answer: $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b} = 3(-2) + 2(1) = -4$.

questions.question: Given $\mathbf{a} = 3\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{b} = -2\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j}$ (so $\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b} = -4$), find $\text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\mathbf{a}$ and express your answer in the form $x\mathbf{i} + y\mathbf{j}$.
questions.answer: $$\text{proj}_{\mathbf{b}}\mathbf{a} = \frac{\mathbf{a}\cdot\mathbf{b}}{\mathbf{b}\cdot\mathbf{b}}\,\mathbf{b} = \frac{-4}{5}(-2\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j}) = \frac{8}{5}\mathbf{i} - \frac{4}{5}\mathbf{j}.$$

questions.question: Ten unbiased six-sided dice are tossed simultaneously. Write an expression for the probability of exactly three of them landing with the number 5 facing up.

questions.question: Given $P(x) = 3x^3 - 2x^2 + x - 3$ has zeroes $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$, and $\alpha\beta\gamma = 1$, find the value of $\dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{\beta} + \dfrac{1}{\gamma}$.
questions.answer: $$\frac{1}{\alpha} + \frac{1}{\beta} + \frac{1}{\gamma} = \frac{\alpha\beta + \alpha\gamma + \beta\gamma}{\alpha\beta\gamma} = \frac{\frac{1}{3}}{1} = \frac{1}{3}.$$

questions.question: The curves $y = |x|$ and $y = \dfrac{82}{25 + 4x^2}$ intersect at the points $(2, 2)$ and $(-2, 2)$. Find the area bounded by the curves, as shown in the diagram. Give your answer correct to one decimal place.
questions.answer:
By symmetry,
$$A = 2\int_0^2\left(\frac{82}{25 + 4x^2} - x\right)dx = 2\left[\frac{82}{4}\cdot\frac{2}{5}\tan^{-1}\frac{2x}{5} - \frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^2 = \frac{82}{5}\tan^{-1}\frac{4}{5} - 4 \approx 7.1 \text{ units}^2.$$

questions.question: Three adults and five children go to the cinema and are seated next to each other in a row of eight seats. How many ways can these eight people sit so that at least two of the adults sit next to each other?
questions.answer:
Total arrangements: $8!$. Arrangements with no two adults together: seat the 5 children ($5!$ ways), creating 6 gaps; place the 3 adults in different gaps in $6 \times 5 \times 4$ ways.
$$8! - 5! \times 6 \times 5 \times 4 = 40320 - 14400 = 25920.$$

questions.answer: $\dfrac{dT}{dt} = kAe^{kt} = k\left(5 + Ae^{kt} - 5\right) = k(T - 5)$.

Find the values of $s$ and $t$ in the following sum of binomial coefficients:
$$\binom{2022}{146} + \binom{2022}{147} + \binom{2023}{1875} = \binom{s}{t}.$$
Prove, by mathematical induction, that $n^3 + (n+1)^3 + (n+2)^3$ is divisible by 9 for all integers $n \ge 1$.
questions.answer:
**$n = 1$:** $1 + 8 + 27 = 36 = 9 \times 4$. True.

**Assume true for $n = k$:** $k^3 + (k+1)^3 + (k+2)^3 = 9m$ for some integer $m$.

**Prove for $n = k + 1$:**
$$(k+1)^3 + (k+2)^3 + (k+3)^3 = 9m - k^3 + (k+3)^3 = 9m + 9k^2 + 27k + 27 = 9(m + k^2 + 3k + 3),$$
which is divisible by 9 since $m + k^2 + 3k + 3$ is an integer. Hence true for all $n \ge 1$ by mathematical induction.

questions.question:
Consider the unit circle centred at the origin $O$, with $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ the standard unit vectors in the horizontal and vertical directions. The points $P$ and $Q$ lie on the unit circle such that $P$ is in the first quadrant and $Q$ is in the fourth quadrant. The angles $POX$ and $QOX$ have measures $\alpha$ and $\beta$ respectively, where $X$ is the point $(1, 0)$. Let $\overrightarrow{OP} = \mathbf{p}$, $\overrightarrow{OQ} = \mathbf{q}$.

Find $\mathbf{p}$ in terms of $\alpha$, and $\mathbf{q}$ in terms of $\beta$.
questions.answer: $\mathbf{p} = \cos\alpha\,\mathbf{i} + \sin\alpha\,\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{q} = \cos\beta\,\mathbf{i} - \sin\beta\,\mathbf{j}$.

questions.question:
Consider the unit circle centred at the origin $O$, with $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ the standard unit vectors in the horizontal and vertical directions. The points $P$ and $Q$ lie on the unit circle such that $P$ is in the first quadrant and $Q$ is in the fourth quadrant. The angles $POX$ and $QOX$ have measures $\alpha$ and $\beta$ respectively, where $X$ is the point $(1, 0)$. Let $\overrightarrow{OP} = \mathbf{p}$, $\overrightarrow{OQ} = \mathbf{q}$. Also $\mathbf{p} = \cos\alpha\,\mathbf{i} + \sin\alpha\,\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{q} = \cos\beta\,\mathbf{i} - \sin\beta\,\mathbf{j}$.

By considering $\mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{q}$, show that $\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta$.
questions.answer:
Componentwise: $\mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{q} = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta$.
The angle between $\mathbf{p}$ and $\mathbf{q}$ is $\alpha + \beta$, and $|\mathbf{p}| = |\mathbf{q}| = 1$, so $\mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{q} = |\mathbf{p}||\mathbf{q}|\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos(\alpha + \beta)$.
Hence $\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta$.

questions.question: Sketch the graphs of $y = |x^2 - 3x + 2|$ and $y = 2$ on the same axes.
questions.answer: $x^2 - 3x + 2 = (x - 1)(x - 2)$. The parabola has $x$-intercepts 1 and 2 and $y$-intercept 2; the part between $x = 1$ and $x = 2$ (minimum $-\frac{1}{4}$ at $x = \frac{3}{2}$) is reflected above the axis, with maximum $\frac{1}{4}$. The line $y = 2$ meets the graph at $x = 0$ and $x = 3$.

questions.question: The graphs of $y = |x^2 - 3x + 2|$ and $y = 2$ meet at $x = 0$ and $x = 3$. Hence, or otherwise, solve $|x^2 - 3x + 2| > 2$.
questions.answer: $x < 0$ or $x > 3$. (Algebraically: $x^2 - 3x + 2 > 2 \Rightarrow x(x - 3) > 0$; and $x^2 - 3x + 2 < -2$ has no solutions since the minimum is $-\frac{1}{4}$.)

questions.question:
Let $\theta$ be the measure of an acute angle. Using a suitable expansion of $\sin 6\theta$, show that
$$(\sin 2\theta)^3 - \frac{3}{4}\sin 2\theta + \frac{1}{4}\sin 6\theta = 0.$$
questions.answer:
$$\sin 6\theta = \sin(4\theta + 2\theta) = \sin 4\theta\cos 2\theta + \cos 4\theta\sin 2\theta = 2\sin 2\theta\cos^2 2\theta + (1 - 2\sin^2 2\theta)\sin 2\theta$$
$$= 2\sin 2\theta(1 - \sin^2 2\theta) + \sin 2\theta - 2\sin^3 2\theta = 3\sin 2\theta - 4\sin^3 2\theta.$$
So LHS $= \sin^3 2\theta - \frac{3}{4}\sin 2\theta + \frac{1}{4}(3\sin 2\theta - 4\sin^3 2\theta) = 0$.

questions.question: It is known that $(\sin 2\theta)^3 - \frac{3}{4}\sin 2\theta + \frac{1}{4}\sin 6\theta = 0$. If $x = 4\sin 2\theta$ and $x^3 - 12x + 8 = 0$, show that $\sin 6\theta = \frac{1}{2}$.
questions.answer:
Substitute: $64\sin^3 2\theta - 48\sin 2\theta + 8 = 0$. Divide by 64: $\sin^3 2\theta - \frac{3}{4}\sin 2\theta + \frac{1}{8} = 0$.
Comparing with the identity, $\sin^3 2\theta - \frac{3}{4}\sin 2\theta = -\frac{1}{4}\sin 6\theta$, so $-\frac{1}{4}\sin 6\theta + \frac{1}{8} = 0$, giving $\sin 6\theta = \frac{1}{2}$.

So LHS $= \sin^3 2\theta - \frac{3}{4}\sin 2\theta + \frac{1}{4}(3\sin 2\theta - 4\sin^3 2\theta) = 0$.

questions.question:
If $x = 4\sin 2\theta$ satisfies $x^3 - 12x + 8 = 0$, then $\sin 6\theta = \frac{1}{2}$. Use this result to find the value of
$$\left(\sin\frac{\pi}{18}\right)^2 + \left(\sin\frac{13\pi}{18}\right)^2 + \left(\sin\frac{25\pi}{18}\right)^2.$$
questions.answer:
$\sin 6\theta = \frac{1}{2}$ gives $6\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{13\pi}{6}, \frac{25\pi}{6}, \dots$, i.e. $2\theta = \frac{\pi}{18}, \frac{13\pi}{18}, \frac{25\pi}{18}$. These give three distinct values of $x = 4\sin 2\theta$, so they are the three roots of $x^3 - 12x + 8 = 0$ (other solutions repeat these values).
Sum of roots $= 0$; sum of products in pairs $= -12$. So
$$\sum x^2 = \left(\sum x\right)^2 - 2\sum x_ix_j = 0 + 24 = 24.$$
Since each $x^2 = 16\sin^2 2\theta$:
$$\sin^2\frac{\pi}{18} + \sin^2\frac{13\pi}{18} + \sin^2\frac{25\pi}{18} = \frac{24}{16} = \frac{3}{2}.$$

questions.question:
Liquid is poured into a large vertical circular cylinder at a constant rate of 1600 cm³ s⁻¹. At the same time, liquid is leaking from a hole in the base of the cylinder at a rate that is proportional to the square root of the height of the liquid in the cylinder. The area of the circular cross-section of the cylinder is 4000 cm².

Show that at time $t$ seconds, the height $h$ cm of liquid in the cylinder satisfies the differential equation
$$\frac{dh}{dt} = 0.4 - c\sqrt{h},$$
where $c$ is a constant.
questions.answer:
$V = 4000h$, so $\frac{dV}{dh} = 4000$. The net rate is $\frac{dV}{dt} = 1600 - k\sqrt{h}$ for some constant $k > 0$.
$$\frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{dV}{dt} \div \frac{dV}{dh} = \frac{1600 - k\sqrt{h}}{4000} = 0.4 - c\sqrt{h}, \quad \text{where } c = \frac{k}{4000}.$$

questions.question:
Liquid is poured into a large vertical circular cylinder at a constant rate of 1600 cm³ s⁻¹. At the same time, liquid is leaking from a hole in the base of the cylinder at a rate that is proportional to the square root of the height of the liquid in the cylinder. The area of the circular cross-section of the cylinder is 4000 cm². The height satisfies $\frac{dh}{dt} = 0.4 - c\sqrt{h}$, where the leak rate is $k\sqrt{h}$ cm³ s⁻¹ and $c = \frac{k}{4000}$.

When $h = 25$ cm, liquid is leaking from the hole at a rate of 400 cm³ s⁻¹. Show that $c = 0.02$.
questions.answer: $k\sqrt{25} = 400 \Rightarrow k = 80$, so $c = \dfrac{80}{4000} = 0.02$.

questions.question: The graphs of $y = (x - 1)^2$ and $y = \sqrt{x - 1}$ intersect at $(1, 0)$ and $P(x, y)$, as shown. Write down the point of intersection $P(x, y)$.

The graphs of $y = (x - 1)^2$ and $y = \sqrt{x - 1}$ intersect at $(1, 0)$ and $(2, 1)$. Find the volume of the solid of revolution formed by rotating the region bounded by $y = \sqrt{x - 1}$ and $y = (x - 1)^2$ about the $y$-axis.
questions.answer:
For $1 \le x \le 2$: $y = (x - 1)^2 \Rightarrow x = 1 + \sqrt{y}$ (outer), and $y = \sqrt{x - 1} \Rightarrow x = 1 + y^2$ (inner), for $0 \le y \le 1$.
$$V = \pi\int_0^1\left[(1 + \sqrt{y})^2 - (1 + y^2)^2\right]dy = \pi\int_0^1\left(2\sqrt{y} + y - 2y^2 - y^4\right)dy$$
$$= \pi\left[\frac{4}{3}y^{3/2} + \frac{y^2}{2} - \frac{2y^3}{3} - \frac{y^5}{5}\right]_0^1 = \pi\left(\frac{4}{3} + \frac{1}{2} - \frac{2}{3} - \frac{1}{5}\right) = \frac{29\pi}{30} \text{ units}^3.$$

questions.question:
Show that
$$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3a^2x - x^3}{a^3 - 3ax^2}\right) = 3\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{a}\right), \quad \text{where } a > 0,\ -\frac{a}{\sqrt{3}} < x < \frac{a}{\sqrt{3}}.$$
Any identity used that is not listed on the reference sheet must be derived.
questions.answer:
Let $\theta = \tan^{-1}\frac{x}{a}$ and $t = \tan\theta = \frac{x}{a}$. Using $\tan(2\theta + \theta)$ and $\tan 2\theta = \frac{2t}{1 - t^2}$:
$$\tan 3\theta = \frac{\frac{2t}{1 - t^2} + t}{1 - \frac{2t^2}{1 - t^2}} = \frac{3t - t^3}{1 - 3t^2} = \frac{3\frac{x}{a} - \frac{x^3}{a^3}}{1 - \frac{3x^2}{a^2}} = \frac{3a^2x - x^3}{a^3 - 3ax^2}.$$
Since $a > 0$ and $-\frac{a}{\sqrt{3}} < x < \frac{a}{\sqrt{3}}$, we have $-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} < \frac{x}{a} < \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, so $-\frac{\pi}{6} < \theta < \frac{\pi}{6}$ and $-\frac{\pi}{2} < 3\theta < \frac{\pi}{2}$ (this also ensures the denominator is non-zero). Therefore $\tan^{-1}(\tan 3\theta) = 3\theta$, and
$$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3a^2x - x^3}{a^3 - 3ax^2}\right) = 3\theta = 3\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{a}.$$

questions.question: Given that $\overrightarrow{AD}=\begin{pmatrix}-2\\3\end{pmatrix}$ and $\overrightarrow{DO}=\begin{pmatrix}6\\-4\end{pmatrix}$, what is $\overrightarrow{OA}$?
questions.answer: $\overrightarrow{AO}=\overrightarrow{AD}+\overrightarrow{DO}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\-1\end{pmatrix}$, so $\overrightarrow{OA}=-\overrightarrow{AO}=\begin{pmatrix}-4\\1\end{pmatrix}$ (A).

questions.question: Consider the polynomial $P(x)=4x^2+5x-10$. When $(2x-a)\times P(x)$ is divided by $(x-1)$ the remainder is $3$. What is the value of $a$?
Which of the following is an anti-derivative of $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{9-4x^2}}$?
questions.answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{9-4x^2}}=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{\frac94-x^2}}$. Using $\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt{a^2-x^2}}=\sin^{-1}\frac xa$ with $a=\frac32$ gives $\frac12\sin^{-1}\frac{x}{3/2}=\frac12\sin^{-1}\frac{2x}3+c$ (A).

questions.question: A factory produces light switches. Each switch has a 6% chance of being faulty. A quality control manager selects a random sample of 80 switches. Let $X$ represent the number of faulty switches in the sample, where $X$ is a binomial variable. What is the standard deviation of $X$, correct to 2 decimal places?
questions.answer: $X\sim\mathrm{Bin}(80,0.06)$, so $\mathrm{Var}(X)=np(1-p)=80(0.06)(0.94)=4.512$ and the standard deviation is $\sqrt{4.512}\approx2.12$ (A).

questions.question: The direction field for a differential equation is shown. Which of the differential equations below could give this direction field?
questions.answer: Test the segments circled in the school's solution. At $(3,-1)$ the segment has positive gradient: A gives $\frac{-1}{-2+3}=-1$, C gives $\frac{-1}{2+3}=-\frac15$, so A and C are ruled out, while B gives $+1$ and D gives $\frac{-1}{-2-3}=+\frac15$. At $(3,-2)$ the segment has negative gradient: D gives $\frac{-2}{-4-3}=+\frac27>0$, so D fails, while B gives $-\frac{-2}{-4+3}=-2<0$ as required. Only B fits both points (B).

questions.question: The vectors $\mathbf d$, $\mathbf u$, $\mathbf b$, $\mathbf o$ are each chosen to be either $\begin{pmatrix}2\\1\end{pmatrix}$ or $\begin{pmatrix}3\\-1\end{pmatrix}$. If each possible selection is equally likely, what is the probability that $\mathbf d+\mathbf u+\mathbf b+\mathbf o=\begin{pmatrix}10\\0\end{pmatrix}$?
questions.answer: Suppose $k$ of the four vectors are $\begin{pmatrix}3\\-1\end{pmatrix}$. The sum is $\begin{pmatrix}2(4-k)+3k\\(4-k)-k\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}8+k\\4-2k\end{pmatrix}$, which equals $\begin{pmatrix}10\\0\end{pmatrix}$ when $k=2$. There are $\binom42=6$ such selections out of $2^4=16$, so the probability is $\frac6{16}=\frac38$ (D).

questions.question: For the vectors $\mathbf a=3\mathbf i+2\mathbf j$ and $\mathbf b=9\mathbf i+3\mathbf j$, which of the following represents $|\mathbf a+\mathbf b|$?
questions.answer: $\mathbf a+\mathbf b=12\mathbf i+5\mathbf j$, so $|\mathbf a+\mathbf b|=\sqrt{144+25}=13$ (D).

questions.question: The function $f(x)$ exists for all real numbers $x$. The function $g(x)$ is defined such that $g(x)=f(x)+\dfrac{1}{f(x)}$. If $f(2)=-1$ and $f'(2)>0$, which of the following is true about $g(x)$?
A first-order differential equation is given by $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2y\ln y$. Which of the following is a solution to the differential equation?
questions.answer: Try $y=e^{e^{2x}}$: $\ln y=e^{2x}$ and $\frac{dy}{dx}=e^{e^{2x}}\cdot2e^{2x}=2y\ln y$ as required (B). (The others fail: for A, $\ln y=2e^x$ gives $2y\ln y=4e^xy$ but $y'=2e^xy$; for C, $y'=2xe^{x^2}y\ne2e^{x^2}y$; for D, $\ln y=\ln2+e^x$ and $y'=e^xy\ne2y\ln y$.)

questions.question: For a particular function $f(x)$, it is known that $f(0)=0$ and $x\times f(x)>0$ for all non-zero values of $x$. It is also known that $\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,dx=4$ and $\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2}|f(x)|\,dx=8$. Which of the following gives the value of $\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{0}f(|x|)\,dx$?
questions.answer: Since $xf(x)>0$, $f(x)>0$ for $x>0$ and $f(x)<0$ for $x<0$. Let $A=\int_0^2f$ and $B=\int_{-2}^0f<0$. Then $A+B=4$ and $\int|f|=A-B=8$, so $A=6$ (and $B=-2$). Now $f(|x|)=f(-x)$ for $x\le0$, so $\int_{-2}^0f(|x|)\,dx=\int_0^2f(x)\,dx=A=6$ (D).

questions.question: For the vectors $\mathbf a=10\mathbf i+2\mathbf j$ and $\mathbf b=\mathbf i-\mathbf j$, evaluate $3\mathbf a-\mathbf b$.
questions.answer: $3\mathbf a-\mathbf b=(30\mathbf i+6\mathbf j)-(\mathbf i-\mathbf j)=29\mathbf i+7\mathbf j$.

questions.question: For the vectors $\mathbf a=10\mathbf i+2\mathbf j$ and $\mathbf b=\mathbf i-\mathbf j$, evaluate $(\mathbf a+2\mathbf b)\cdot(\mathbf a-2\mathbf b)$.
questions.answer: $\mathbf a+2\mathbf b=12\mathbf i+0\mathbf j$ and $\mathbf a-2\mathbf b=8\mathbf i+4\mathbf j$. The dot product is $12\times8+0\times4=96$. (Check: $(\mathbf a+2\mathbf b)\cdot(\mathbf a-2\mathbf b)=|\mathbf a|^2-4|\mathbf b|^2=104-8=96$.)

questions.question: Using the substitution $u=x+4$, find the exact value of $\displaystyle\int_{-4}^{-3}x(x+4)^{10}\,dx$.
In how many different ways can all the letters of the word TENNANT be arranged in a line?
questions.answer: There are 7 letters, with T repeated 2 times and N repeated 3 times (E and A once each). The number of arrangements is $\dfrac{7!}{2!\,3!}=\dfrac{5040}{12}=420$.

questions.question: Find the constant term in the expansion of $\left(2x-\dfrac1x\right)^{10}$.
questions.answer: The general term is $T_k=\binom{10}{k}(2x)^k\left(-\frac1x\right)^{10-k}=\binom{10}{k}2^k(-1)^{10-k}x^{2k-10}$. The constant term needs $2k-10=0$, so $k=5$: $\binom{10}{5}2^5(-1)^5=252\times32\times(-1)=-8064$.

questions.question: Solve $\sqrt2\cos\left(x+\dfrac\pi4\right)+\sqrt2\cos\left(x-\dfrac\pi4\right)=1$ for $-\pi\le x\le\pi$.
questions.answer: Expand: $\cos\left(x+\frac\pi4\right)+\cos\left(x-\frac\pi4\right)=2\cos x\cos\frac\pi4=\sqrt2\cos x$. So the left side is $\sqrt2\times\sqrt2\cos x=2\cos x$. Then $2\cos x=1$, $\cos x=\frac12$, giving $x=\pm\dfrac\pi3$.

questions.question: Show that $\sec^2\left(\dfrac\pi4-\dfrac x2\right)=\dfrac{2}{1+\sin x}$.
questions.answer: $\sec^2\theta=\dfrac1{\cos^2\theta}$ and $\cos^2\theta=\frac12(1+\cos2\theta)$. With $\theta=\frac\pi4-\frac x2$, $2\theta=\frac\pi2-x$ and $\cos2\theta=\cos\left(\frac\pi2-x\right)=\sin x$. So $\sec^2\theta=\dfrac{2}{1+\sin x}$.

questions.question: Using $\sec^2\left(\dfrac\pi4-\dfrac x2\right)=\dfrac{2}{1+\sin x}$, evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^\pi\dfrac{2}{1+\sin x}\,dx$.
questions.answer: $\int_0^\pi\sec^2\left(\frac\pi4-\frac x2\right)dx=\left[-2\tan\left(\frac\pi4-\frac x2\right)\right]_0^\pi=-2\tan\left(-\frac\pi4\right)+2\tan\frac\pi4=2+2=4$.

prev.question: Show that $\sec^2\left(\dfrac\pi4-\dfrac x2\right)=\dfrac{2}{1+\sin x}$.
prev.answer: $\sec^2\theta=\dfrac1{\cos^2\theta}$ and $\cos^2\theta=\frac12(1+\cos2\theta)$. With $\theta=\frac\pi4-\frac x2$, $2\theta=\frac\pi2-x$ and $\cos2\theta=\cos\left(\frac\pi2-x\right)=\sin x$. So $\sec^2\theta=\dfrac{2}{1+\sin x}$.

questions.question: The volume of a cylinder with a fixed height $h$ cm and radius $r$ cm is given by $V=\pi r^2h$. If the volume is increasing at a rate of $20\ \text{cm}^3\,\text{s}^{-1}$, show that $\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{10}{\pi rh}\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$.
questions.answer: $\frac{dV}{dr}=2\pi rh$ (as $h$ is constant). By the chain rule, $\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{dV}{dr}\cdot\frac{dr}{dt}$, so $20=2\pi rh\frac{dr}{dt}$ and $\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{10}{\pi rh}$.

questions.question: The region $D$ is bounded by the $y$-axis, the $x$-axis, the line $x=\ln4$ and the curve $y=e^x+2e^{-x}$, as shown in the diagram. Find the exact volume of the solid formed when $D$ is rotated about the $x$-axis.
questions.answer: $V=\pi\int_0^{\ln4}\left(e^x+2e^{-x}\right)^2dx=\pi\int_0^{\ln4}\left(e^{2x}+4+4e^{-2x}\right)dx=\pi\left[\tfrac12e^{2x}+4x-2e^{-2x}\right]_0^{\ln4}$. At $x=\ln4$: $\tfrac12(16)+4\ln4-2\left(\tfrac1{16}\right)=8+4\ln4-\tfrac18$. At $x=0$: $\tfrac12-2=-\tfrac32$. So $V=\pi\left(8+4\ln4-\tfrac18+\tfrac32\right)=\pi\left(\dfrac{75}8+4\ln4\right)$ cubic units.

questions.question: The polynomial $P(x)=8x^4-38x^3+9x^2+ax+b$ has a double root at $x=3$. Find the values of $a$ and $b$.
Use mathematical induction to show that for all integers $n\ge1$, $4^{2n}-1$ is divisible by $3$.
questions.answer: Let $S(n)$: $4^{2n}-1$ is divisible by 3. **Base case** $n=1$: $4^2-1=15=3\times5$, so $S(1)$ is true. **Inductive step:** assume $S(k)$ is true for some integer $k\ge1$, i.e. $4^{2k}-1=3m$ for an integer $m$, so $4^{2k}=3m+1$. Then $4^{2(k+1)}-1=16\cdot4^{2k}-1=16(3m+1)-1=48m+15=3(16m+5)$, which is divisible by 3 since $16m+5$ is an integer. So $S(k)\Rightarrow S(k+1)$. By induction, $S(n)$ is true for all integers $n\ge1$.

questions.question: Consider the function $f(x)=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x+1}\right)$ for $-\dfrac\pi2<x<\dfrac\pi2$. Find $f'(x)$.
questions.answer: Let $g=\frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}$. By the quotient rule, $g'=\frac{-\sin x(1+\sin x)-\cos^2x}{(1+\sin x)^2}=\frac{-\sin x-1}{(1+\sin x)^2}=\frac{-1}{1+\sin x}$. Also $1+g^2=\frac{(1+\sin x)^2+\cos^2x}{(1+\sin x)^2}=\frac{2+2\sin x}{(1+\sin x)^2}=\frac2{1+\sin x}$. Then $f'(x)=\frac{g'}{1+g^2}=\frac{-1}{1+\sin x}\times\frac{1+\sin x}{2}=-\dfrac12$.

questions.question: Let $f(x)=\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x+1}\right)$ for $-\dfrac\pi2<x<\dfrac\pi2$, and suppose $f'(x)=-\dfrac12$ for all $x$ in this domain. Hence sketch the graph of $y=f(x)$.
questions.answer: Since $f'(x)=-\frac12$, $f(x)=-\frac12x+C$. At $x=0$, $f(0)=\tan^{-1}(1)=\frac\pi4$, so $C=\frac\pi4$ and $f(x)=\frac\pi4-\frac x2$. The graph is a straight line of gradient $-\frac12$ with open endpoints $\left(-\frac\pi2,\frac\pi2\right)$ and $\left(\frac\pi2,0\right)$, passing through $\left(0,\frac\pi4\right)$ (see graph).

prev.answer: Let $g=\frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}$. By the quotient rule, $g'=\frac{-\sin x(1+\sin x)-\cos^2x}{(1+\sin x)^2}=\frac{-\sin x-1}{(1+\sin x)^2}=\frac{-1}{1+\sin x}$. questions.question: Solve the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x\sqrt{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}$ given that it passes through the point $(1,0)$. Give your answer with $y$ as the subject.
questions.answer: Separate variables: $\int\frac{dy}{\sqrt{1-y^2}}=\int x\sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx$. The left side is $\sin^{-1}y$. For the right side, $\int x(1-x^2)^{1/2}dx=-\frac12\cdot\frac{(1-x^2)^{3/2}}{3/2}=-\frac13(1-x^2)^{3/2}$. So $\sin^{-1}y=-\frac13(1-x^2)^{3/2}+C$. At $(1,0)$: $0=0+C$, so $C=0$. Therefore $y=\sin\left(-\dfrac13(1-x^2)^{3/2}\right)=-\sin\left(\dfrac{(1-x^2)^{3/2}}3\right)$.

questions.question: Prove that $\dfrac{1}{\binom{2025}{26}}=\dfrac{26}{25}\left(\dfrac1{\binom{2024}{25}}-\dfrac1{\binom{2025}{25}}\right)$.

Ecologists are re-introducing 3000 Komodo dragons to an island. Populations of more than 3000 are unsustainable. They model population growth by $\dfrac{dK}{dt}=rK(3000-K)$, where $K$ is the number of Komodo dragons on the island, $t$ is the time in years and $r$ is a constant. Ecologists know that when the maximum growth rate occurs, all the Komodo dragons find a mate, and half of these pairs successfully raise one juvenile Komodo dragon. Show that $r=\dfrac1{6000}$.
questions.answer: The growth rate $rK(3000-K)$ is largest at the vertex of this quadratic in $K$, i.e. $K=1500$, where $\frac{dK}{dt}=r(1500)(1500)=2\,250\,000\,r$. At this population the 1500 dragons form 750 pairs, and half of these (375 pairs) raise one juvenile each, so the population grows by 375 per year. Hence $2\,250\,000\,r=375$ and $r=\dfrac{375}{2\,250\,000}=\dfrac1{6000}$.

questions.question: A population of Komodo dragons satisfies $\dfrac{dK}{dt}=\dfrac{K(3000-K)}{6000}$, with $K=500$ when $t=0$. Use the fact that $\dfrac1{K(3000-K)}=\dfrac1{3000}\left(\dfrac1K+\dfrac1{3000-K}\right)$ to show that $K=\dfrac{3000}{5e^{-0.5t}+1}$.
questions.answer: Separate: $\int\frac{dK}{K(3000-K)}=\int\frac{dt}{6000}$. Using the given partial fractions, $\frac1{3000}\left(\ln K-\ln(3000-K)\right)=\frac t{6000}+c$ (for $0<K<3000$), so $\ln\frac K{3000-K}=\frac t2+C$. At $t=0$, $K=500$: $\ln\frac{500}{2500}=\ln\frac15=C$. So $\frac K{3000-K}=\frac15e^{t/2}$, i.e. $\frac{3000-K}K=5e^{-0.5t}$. Then $3000-K=5Ke^{-0.5t}$, so $3000=K\left(5e^{-0.5t}+1\right)$ and $K=\dfrac{3000}{5e^{-0.5t}+1}$.

questions.question: Particle $A$ is projected from the top of a vertical tower of height $H$ metres with initial speed $v\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ at an acute angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal. At the same time, from a point $D$ metres horizontally from the base of the tower, particle $B$ is projected with initial speed $u\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ at an acute angle $\beta$ to the horizontal (see diagram). Taking the base of the tower as the origin, the positions at time $t$ after launch are $\mathbf r_A=\begin{pmatrix}vt\cos\alpha\\vt\sin\alpha-\frac g2t^2+H\end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf r_B=\begin{pmatrix}ut\cos\beta+D\\ut\sin\beta-\frac g2t^2\end{pmatrix}$ (do not prove these). It is known that $u\sin\beta>v\sin\alpha$ (do not prove this). Show that for the two particles to collide before either reaches the ground, $2u\sin\beta\,(u\sin\beta-v\sin\alpha)>gH$.
questions.answer: The particles collide when $\mathbf r_A=\mathbf r_B$; equating vertical positions: $vt\sin\alpha+H=ut\sin\beta$, so $H=t(u\sin\beta-v\sin\alpha)$ and the collision time is $t=\frac{H}{u\sin\beta-v\sin\alpha}$. Particle $B$ is at height $y_B=t\left(u\sin\beta-\frac g2t\right)$, which is positive (so $B$, and hence $A$ at the collision point, is still airborne) exactly when $t<\frac{2u\sin\beta}g$. So for the collision to occur before either reaches the ground, $\frac H{u\sin\beta-v\sin\alpha}<\frac{2u\sin\beta}g$. Since $u\sin\beta-v\sin\alpha>0$ we may multiply through without reversing the inequality: $gH<2u\sin\beta\,(u\sin\beta-v\sin\alpha)$, as required.

questions.question: Show, by expanding the right-hand side, that $\sin(2\beta)+\cos(2\beta)=\sqrt2\sin\left(2\beta+\dfrac\pi4\right)$.
questions.answer: $\sqrt2\sin\left(2\beta+\frac\pi4\right)=\sqrt2\left(\sin2\beta\cos\frac\pi4+\cos2\beta\sin\frac\pi4\right)=\sqrt2\left(\frac{\sqrt2}2\sin2\beta+\frac{\sqrt2}2\cos2\beta\right)=\sin2\beta+\cos2\beta$.

questions.question: Two particles are projected as follows (as in the situation where $\mathbf r_A=\begin{pmatrix}vt\cos\alpha\\vt\sin\alpha-\frac g2t^2+H\end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf r_B=\begin{pmatrix}ut\cos\beta+D\\ut\sin\beta-\frac g2t^2\end{pmatrix}$), with $u=v$, $H=\dfrac{u^2}g$ and $\alpha=\dfrac\pi2-\beta$, where $\alpha,\beta$ are acute. It is known that if the particles collide before hitting the ground then $2u\sin\beta\,(u\sin\beta-v\sin\alpha)>gH$. Using this and $\sin(2\beta)+\cos(2\beta)=\sqrt2\sin\left(2\beta+\frac\pi4\right)$, show that $\dfrac{3\pi}8<\beta<\dfrac\pi2$ if the two particles collide before hitting the ground.
questions.answer: Substitute: $2u\sin\beta\left(u\sin\beta-u\sin\left(\frac\pi2-\beta\right)\right)>g\cdot\frac{u^2}g$, i.e. $2\sin\beta(\sin\beta-\cos\beta)>1$ (dividing by $u^2$). So $2\sin^2\beta-2\sin\beta\cos\beta>1$. Using $2\sin^2\beta=1-\cos2\beta$ and $2\sin\beta\cos\beta=\sin2\beta$: $1-\cos2\beta-\sin2\beta>1$, so $\sin2\beta+\cos2\beta<0$, i.e. $\sqrt2\sin\left(2\beta+\frac\pi4\right)<0$, so $\sin\left(2\beta+\frac\pi4\right)<0$. As $\beta$ is acute, $2\beta+\frac\pi4\in\left(\frac\pi4,\frac{5\pi}4\right)$, where sine is negative only for $\pi<2\beta+\frac\pi4<\frac{5\pi}4$. Hence $\frac{3\pi}4<2\beta<\pi$, giving $\dfrac{3\pi}8<\beta<\dfrac\pi2$.

questions.question: Three different points $O$, $V$ and $U$ form an isosceles triangle with $|\overrightarrow{OV}|=|\overrightarrow{OU}|=1$. The points $C$ and $D$ are chosen so that $\overrightarrow{VC}=\overrightarrow{CD}=\overrightarrow{DU}=\frac13\overrightarrow{VU}$ (they split $VU$ into thirds). Let $\mathbf v=\overrightarrow{OV}$ and $\mathbf u=\overrightarrow{OU}$, as shown in the diagram. Show that $\overrightarrow{VD}=\frac23\mathbf u-\frac23\mathbf v$ and $\overrightarrow{UC}=\frac23\mathbf v-\frac23\mathbf u$.
questions.answer: $\overrightarrow{VU}=\mathbf u-\mathbf v$. $D$ is two thirds of the way from $V$ to $U$, so $\overrightarrow{VD}=\frac23\overrightarrow{VU}=\frac23\mathbf u-\frac23\mathbf v$. Similarly $\overrightarrow{UV}=\mathbf v-\mathbf u$ and $C$ is two thirds of the way from $U$ to $V$, so $\overrightarrow{UC}=\frac23(\mathbf v-\mathbf u)=\frac23\mathbf v-\frac23\mathbf u$.

questions.question: Three different points $O$, $V$ and $U$ form an isosceles triangle with $|\overrightarrow{OV}|=|\overrightarrow{OU}|=1$. The points $C$ and $D$ are chosen so that $\overrightarrow{VC}=\overrightarrow{CD}=\overrightarrow{DU}=\frac13\overrightarrow{VU}$ (they split $VU$ into thirds). Let $\mathbf v=\overrightarrow{OV}$ and $\mathbf u=\overrightarrow{OU}$, as shown in the diagram. The point $A$ lies on $OV$ such that $\overrightarrow{OA}=\lambda\mathbf v$ with $0<\lambda<1$. Show that $\overrightarrow{AD}=\frac23\mathbf u+\left(\frac13-\lambda\right)\mathbf v$.
questions.answer: $\overrightarrow{AV}=\overrightarrow{OV}-\overrightarrow{OA}=(1-\lambda)\mathbf v$. Then $\overrightarrow{AD}=\overrightarrow{AV}+\overrightarrow{VD}=(1-\lambda)\mathbf v+\frac23\mathbf u-\frac23\mathbf v=\frac23\mathbf u+\left(\frac13-\lambda\right)\mathbf v$.
